newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Big NZ dlr drop fails to ignite NZ wool prices.
newsitem.headline: Big NZ dlr drop fails to ignite NZ wool prices.

text.p: A big fall in the New Zealand dollar failed to translate into a big lift in wool prices in morning trading at woolsales at Napier and Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
In Christchurch the market indicator was 488 cents/kg, up 25 cents on last sale of the past season in June, while in Napier the market indicator was 470 cents/kg.
Wrightson's regional wool manager in Napier Richard Wakeland said prices were lower than expected and the full effect of the lower exchange rate was not yet coming through.
The New Zealand dollar has depreciated over 10 percent against the U.S. dollar since its peak of 71.5 U.S. cents in November last year.
On offer was a total of 4,178 clean tonnes in 35,410 bales, comprising 32 percent second shear, 25 percent crossbred fleece, 11 percent crutchings and 10 percent halfbred fleece.

The remainder included seven percent second shear bellies and pieces, five percent bulky skirtings, four percent lambswool and two percent merino fleece, with the balance made up of miscellaneous wools.

Compared with sales at Napier and Christchurch on June 26, merino fleece was generally seven to 10 percent dearer; halfbred fleece 26 to 27 micron three to five percent dearer, and 28 and 32 micron one to three percent dearer; crossbred fleece 37 micron and finer was the same to five percent dearer, and 38 micron and stronger the same to 1.5 percent cheaper.
Second shear 37 micron and finer was 2.5 to 7.5 percent dearer, and 38 micron and stronger generally unchanged; first lambs, crutchings and bulky skirtings were also generally unchanged.

Exporters reported their major inquiry was coming from western Europe, China and local mills with support from India and Pakistan. Of the total offered so far, 3,344 bales, or 23 percent, had failed to meet grower reserve prices.
